comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the anchor-free word match keeps FALSE claims BLOCKING and mints a fabricated citation — reproducible with any short ticket line (heading/bullet)**

`wordOverlap` (js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:310) uses the overlap coefficient alone: `inter / Math.min(claimWords, lineWords)`. For a 1–2-word ticket line the denominator is the line, so **any** line whose few content words all appear in the claim scores 1.0 ≥ `TICKET_WORD_MATCH_MIN_OVERLAP` (0.6, js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:241) and `claimLineMatch` (js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:326-329) confirms it **without any anchor**. Markdown tickets are full of 1–2-word lines (headings, bullets), so a claim the ticket never makes is "verified".

Reproduced end-to-end through the production sanitizer (`node`, current HEAD):

```text
ticket.md:
  # Payment service
  ## Error handling
  Retries use exponential backoff with a 5 second cap.

claim (uncited spec claim): "According to the ticket, error handling must redact
card numbers from every log line."   ← the ticket NEVER says this

sanitizeReviewData(...) with { ticketText }:
  downgrades: 0
  severity kept: BLOCKING
  census blocking: 1 | recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES
  citation minted: [{"path":"src/payment.js","line":42,"citation":"ticket.md:3"}]

posted body:
  🚨 BLOCKING: According to the ticket, error handling must redact card numbers ...
  Source: ticket.md:3 — requirement verified against the ticket text (gh-1334 citation auto-append).
```

`ticket.md:3` is just the heading `## Error handling` — the auto-appended "requirement verified against the ticket text" line is **false evidence**: downstream triage and the machine treat it as ground truth, the census holds, and rework arms on a possibly-green PR — exactly the gh-1053 pathology, but now with a citation that *looks* authoritative and is harder to disprove. A bullet fixture fails the same way: claim "idempotency keys must rotate daily and be stored hashed" is confirmed by the bare line `- idempotency keys` (citation `ticket.md:3`).

Note the sibling function in this same repo already documents this exact failure mode and guards against it — `js/common/findingRegistry.js:205-206`: *"Jaccard alone punishes subset paraphrases; the overlap coefficient alone overates tiny sets"* — which is why `claimSimilarity` uses the mean of Jaccard and overlap.

**Suggested fix** (validated against this PR's own fixtures): gate the anchor-free path on the *line's* content-word count — a line must itself be requirement-shaped to confirm a claim on words alone:

```javascript
function claimLineMatch(claimWords, normalizedLine, lineNo, anchorCount) {
    var overlap = wordOverlap(claimWords, findingRegistry.contentWords(normalizedLine));
    var matched = (anchorCount > 0 && overlap >= TICKET_ANCHOR_MIN_WORD_OVERLAP) ||
        (overlap >= TICKET_WORD_MATCH_MIN_OVERLAP &&
         findingRegistry.contentWords(normalizedLine).length >= TICKET_MIN_CLAIM_WORDS);
    ...
}
```

With the floor, both repro claims fall to `no` (anchor unseen anywhere, ≥3 claim words → confidently absent → demote as today), while every existing `matchClaimInTicket` fixture still passes: AC1/AC4 lines carry 9 content words, the best-line fixtures 7–9, and the near-identical no-anchor fixture 9. Consider floored line length for the anchored path too (a bare `401` on a 2-word line still passes today, js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:328) — at minimum please add a negative test pinning "a 1–2-word ticket line never confirms an anchor-free claim".

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: stale contract doc — a demoted verdict can never carry `claimMatchedTicket: 'yes'`**

The rewritten docstring of `classifyFindingSeverity` (js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:454-456) documents the demoted branch as:

```text
- demoted → { ..., claimMatchedTicket: 'yes'|'no'|'inconclusive' }
  ('yes' here means the anchor was seen but the line did not qualify — ...)
```

That value is unreachable: `ticketMatchVerdict` (js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:366-374) returns `yes` only when a line actually matched (`scan.best`), and `verifiedOrDemotedVerdict` (js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:443-456) maps `yes` to the `claimVerified` keep-BLOCKING branch. The "anchor seen but the line did not qualify" case returns `inconclusive` (`scan.anchorSeen` → `inconclusiveMatch()`), so a demotion can only ever carry `no` or `inconclusive`. This module is a machine-parsed contract (the marker payload and the registry read these values) — please correct the doc so future consumers don't implement against an impossible state.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: escalation packet lists demotions for resolved identities too — goes stale on long-lived PRs**

`demotionRecords` (js/common/findingRegistry.js:847-858) filters only on `!!i.demotion` — a demoted identity that was later **fixed** or **withdrawn** still shows up in every escalation packet, and `buildEscalationPacketComment` (js/common/findingRegistry.js:884-888) renders it without the status: `⚠️ F3 (src/auth.ts) demoted from BLOCKING — ... (a cited re-raise re-elevates it)` — an instruction that no longer applies to a resolved item.

`buildFindingsInjection` already renders its demotion guidance from `openItems` only (js/common/findingRegistry.js:951), so the two renders disagree. Consider filtering `demotionRecords` to open statuses (or rendering `d.status` in the packet line). The structured packet does carry `status`, but the human-facing comment ignores it.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `registryClaimOf` truncates reviewer claims that legitimately contain a `---` horizontal rule**

`registryClaimOf` (js/postPRReviewComments.js:1057-1059) strips the machine-appended demotion tail by splitting on the generic separator:

```javascript
return String(claim || '').split('\n---\n')[0];
```

The demotion tail is `'\n' + downgradeNote(...)` where `downgradeNote` starts with `'---\n'` — so splitting on `'\n---\n'` works for machine output, but it applies to **every** claim, including clean ones. A reviewer-authored multi-paragraph claim containing a markdown horizontal rule (`\n---\n`) loses everything after the rule in the registry identity — similarity for cross-round dedup is then computed on truncated text, weakening gh-1332 matching.

Stripping only the known machine tail would be precise and loss-free: cut at the first occurrence of `'\n---\n⚠️ **Severity demoted'` (or of the `dmtools:demoted-from-BLOCKING` marker prefix, already exported as `reviewSpecClaims.DEMOTION_MARKER_PREFIX`). Edge case — identity matching only, no posting impact; the new tests pin only the demotion-tail shape.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One 🚨 BLOCKING: the new gh-1334 ticket-verification matcher keeps FALSE uncited claims BLOCKING and auto-appends a fabricated "requirement verified" citation when the ticket has a 1–2-word line (heading/bullet) sharing its words with the claim — reproduced end-to-end through `sanitizeReviewData`. Verified otherwise: canonical suite 8274/0 green, `crap4js` ratchet exit 0 (0 regressions vs released baseline), duplication ratchet OK, `snapshots/pr_review.md` fresh, no open threads from earlier rounds.

**Key Issues**:
1. 🚨 `js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:310` — overlap-coefficient-only match (`min()` denominator) → false "keep BLOCKING" + fabricated `Source: ticket.md:N` citation; `findingRegistry.js:205-206` documents this exact failure mode and guards against it via mean(Jaccard, overlap). Fix: floor the anchor-free path on the ticket line's content-word count (validated against this PR's fixtures).
2. 💡 `js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js:454` — docstring documents an unreachable `claimMatchedTicket: 'yes'` on demotions (machine-parsed contract).
3. 💡 `js/common/findingRegistry.js:847` — escalation packet lists demotions of resolved (fixed/withdrawn) identities; injection renders open-only — renders disagree.
4. 💡 `js/postPRReviewComments.js:1057` — `registryClaimOf` splits on the generic `\n---\n`, truncating reviewer claims that legitimately contain a horizontal rule.

**Next Steps**:
1. Floor the anchor-free word match on the ticket line's content-word count (≥ `TICKET_MIN_CLAIM_WORDS`) and add the negative test "a 1–2-word ticket line never confirms an anchor-free claim".
2. Correct the `classifyFindingSeverity` docstring (drop `yes` from the demoted branch).
3. Filter `demotionRecords` to open statuses or render status in the packet line.
4. Strip only the machine tail (marker prefix) instead of the generic `\n---\n` separator.
